A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FRISM, with matching methods and retained experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-merging evaluations, efficiency measurements, ablations, keyword analyses, and qualitative examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, comparison models, component ablations, and a failure case.

M1.justification: FRISM retains SVD decomposition, frozen task-vector bases, learnable sigmoid gates, and the visual-distillation plus injection-strength objective. Softplus and random-mask variants are added as ablation controls; they do not replace the proposed method. The low-rank variant already appears in v1.

E1.justification: V2 retains the six reasoning benchmarks and three original perception benchmarks, adding OCRBench, MME-Perception, and ChartQA in Appendix D.1/Table A2. These substantially extend evaluation of text recognition, general visual perception, and chart understanding. VizWiz calibration coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated comparisons with OpenVLThinker-7B and VLAA-Thinker-Qwen2.5VL-7B in Tables A2–A3, substantially broadening comparison with post-trained reasoning VLMs. DRIFT and the original merging baselines remain; the original comparison tables are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 changes the reported Task Arithmetic grid from {0.1, 0.2, 0.3} to {0.1, 0.15, 0.2}, matching values already tabulated in v1. FRISM's coefficient described as usually near 0.2 becomes an explicit search over the latter grid. Tables A2–A3 introduce base-normalized benchmark averages. These reported revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained layer-wise and injection-loss ablations, v2 tests bounded sigmoid versus Softplus gates and SVD versus random-mask decomposition in Tables 5–6. Appendix K/Fig. A4 adds a concrete overthinking failure case, complementing the retained successful example and attention analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The new normalized averages summarize benchmark performance rather than uncertainty.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–4, Llama results, and keyword counts retain their values. Substantial new results include 7B MathVista scores of 70.3 for sigmoid versus 68.8 for Softplus, and 3B scores of 45.0 for SVD versus 41.3 for random masks. Table A2 adds benchmark and comparator scores, reporting FRISM's normalized reasoning/perception averages as 104.2%/99.6% of the base.

T1.justification: V2 corrects Eq. 13 by restoring the multiplicative lambda_i factor in the loss derivative, bringing the main text into agreement with the derivative already present in v1 Appendix G.1. The substantive appendix assumptions and derivations are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces reasoning encoded in distinct subspaces with differing subspace contributions, and qualifies visual preservation from 'without compromising' to 'largely preserving.' The contribution statement shifts from identifying reasoning-dominant components to adaptive reweighting under a preservation objective. The central label-free merging contribution remains.

C2.justification: V1's limitations emphasize training cost and architecture compatibility. V2 adds substantive qualifications about longer outputs and inference cost, overthinking failures, the indirect nature of the magnitude-based reasoning objective, and incomplete theoretical understanding. It retains the compatibility restriction and adds an explanation of why bounded gates can limit visual drift and subspace dominance.

D1.justification: Table A1 adds checkpoint identifiers for DRIFT, OpenVLThinker, and VLAA-Thinker. Table A3 newly specifies GPU counts—one for FRISM and eight for the listed post-training methods—and additional training-time information. These extend reproducibility and resource documentation without establishing changes to FRISM's implementation.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for the new benchmarks and comparison models, plus LSSF and multimodal KV-cache compression work supporting its motivation. The related-work organization and positioning against existing merging approaches remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and notation edits, corrects reported improvements from percentages to points, and adds Section 4.5, acknowledgements, and an impact statement. Appendix D consolidates additional experiments, with subsequent sections relabeled. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: New Tables 5–6 and A2–A3 substantially expand displays of component ablations, reasoning/perception comparisons, and efficiency; Fig. A4 adds a failure panel. Existing figures and case-study boxes are retained. The attention visualization moves from v1's final page to Fig. A3 beside its discussion, alongside table, caption, and appendix-label adjustments.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens an already extensive empirical study through targeted component controls and broader perception and post-training comparisons. Its qualified abstract and explicit overthinking, inference-cost, and proxy-objective limitations provide a more balanced account than v1. These are useful incremental gains; the small new comparative advantages still lack uncertainty estimates, and the underlying mechanism analysis is largely unchanged.
